title: The pillar with no end
hookLine: a night kept awake, water poured over the lingam, Om Namah Shivaya until dawn
carry: no top, no bottom: shiva is endless

cards: Two gods are arguing. Brahma, the creator, says: I made everything, so I'm the greatest. Vishnu, the preserver, says: I hold everything together, so I am.
It's an argument you could hear at any dinner table: who matters most. And it's getting heated. Then, between them, out of nowhere, a column of fire bursts up out of the ground.
It rises past the clouds and goes down past anything they can see. No top, no bottom. Both of them stop talking.

teach.h: A BOAR DIGS, A SWAN FLIES.
teach.b: This story is told in the Shiva Purana, and in others too.
The two gods make a deal: whoever finds the end of the pillar wins. Vishnu becomes a boar and digs down. Brahma becomes a swan and flies up.
They go for what the story calls ages. Vishnu never reaches the bottom. He comes back and says, honestly: I couldn't find it.
Brahma never reaches the top. On the way he sees a flower drifting down, and in many tellings he takes it back as proof and claims he found the top. He didn't.
Then the pillar opens, and Shiva steps out of it. The light was him all along. In the tellings, Vishnu is honored for his honesty, and Brahma is rebuked for the lie.
This is one of the stories people tell about the lingam, the rounded stone at the heart of a Shiva temple. Some understand it as a small image of that pillar of light: no beginning, no end.
Some say this is the night it happened, the great night of Shiva. Now the teaching. The argument was about who was biggest.
The answer was something neither god could measure. For Shiva's devotees, he isn't one more god in the lineup; he's the endless reality the gods themselves come from.

teach.h: THE LINGAM: A FORM FOR THE FORMLESS.
teach.b: That's why the lingam has no face: a form for the one beyond form. And the two gods? Brahma's pride wanted to say, I reached the end.
Vishnu's honest I couldn't was the right answer to the infinite.

how: On Maha Shivaratri many Hindus fast, keep a night-long vigil in Shiva temples, pour water, milk and bilva leaves over the lingam, and chant Om Namah Shivaya; many temple carvings show Shiva appearing from the pillar of light.

o: a dawn hymn sung to Shiva

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: became a boar and dug down
became a swan and flew up
fire with no top and no bottom
many see it as that pillar of light

s: Vishnu found the bottom of the pillar
he never reached it, and came back and said so honestly.
in many tellings, Brahma claims he found the top
he brings back a flower as proof. he's rebuked for the lie.
in the story, Shiva steps out of the pillar
the pillar opens, and he appears. the light was him all along.

games.q: you're Vishnu. you've dug for ages and never found the bottom of the pillar. Brahma is coming back. what do you do?
o: say you found it, to win the argument.
admit you couldn't find the end.
keep digging and never go back.
games.why: he admits it honestly. in the tellings, Shiva honors him for it, and rebukes Brahma, who lied.

practice: On this night many Hindus pour water over the lingam and repeat Om Namah Shivaya, I bow to Shiva. If you pray, say it softly eleven times, or pour a glass of water slowly as an offering.
If you don't, picture the pillar of light, rising and sinking farther than you can follow. When the voice comes that says that's enough, take three more breaths.

wordCard.voice: Shivaratri. The great night of Shiva. For many, the night the pillar of light appeared, with no top and no bottom.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the emergence from the linga, the name for this story and its temple image.

carryVoice: Your line: no top, no bottom: Shiva is endless. Neither god could measure him. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Shiva Purana, Vidyeshvara Samhita (the pillar of fire, Brahma and Vishnu)
